concerns.message: filterBy(['code']) with a code generated on the server is fragile. Colyseus fills the filterBy fields of a room's listing from the client's create options, not from values set in onCreate. A code generated in onCreate is therefore not in the listing unless the room writes `this.listing.code` itself. Two more traps: a room marked with `setPrivate()` (the word 'private' invites it) is left out of `join()` queries, and a full room is locked and also left out.
concerns.consequence: Joining by code always fails with 'no rooms found' until the worker finds the listing detail. Even after that, a ninth player who joins a full room is told 'No match with that code' instead of a 'match is full' refusal, because matchmaking cannot tell a full room from an unknown code. The integration test or a reviewer will catch this late.

concerns.message: Package resolution when nothing is built yet. The verifier runs typecheck, unit and integration before build in a clean worktree, and dist/ is gitignored. The Playwright web servers must also start without a prior build. If a workspace's package.json `exports` or `main` points at dist/, checks pass in the worker's worktree, where dist/ is left over from earlier builds, and fail at the verifier. The server's build output also has to work at runtime: Node 24 type stripping does not handle workspace TypeScript imported without `.ts` extensions.
concerns.consequence: A green local run turns into a verifier failure and uses one of the three verification attempts. The fix then means rewiring package exports across all six workspaces.

concerns.message: The rule allowing the previous major for 'that one package' does not fit Colyseus. The server (`colyseus`/`@colyseus/core`), `@colyseus/schema` and the client SDK are versioned as a set. `@colyseus/sdk` is, as far as I know, the 0.17-era name; the 0.16 client was `colyseus.js`. Falling back to the previous version of only one of them does not work.
concerns.consequence: If 0.17 misbehaves on Node 24, the worker might pair a 0.16 server with the 0.17 SDK (handshake or schema decode failures), or report `blocked` even though the matched 0.16 set would work. The decision's wording ("decodes with @colyseus/sdk") would then also be wrong.

concerns.message: Schema decorators and class fields. With `@type()` decorators and `useDefineForClassFields` on (the default for ES2022+ targets, and what esbuild/oxc in Vitest and Vite follow), class field initialisers overwrite the accessors the decorators install. Mutations then stop producing patches, and no error is raised. Whether the TypeScript version the task calls current stable still supports legacy `experimentalDecorators` is a further risk.
concerns.consequence: Ship positions change on the server but never reach clients. The integration and two-ships-sync tests time out and give no clear cause, which can cost hours. The schema() or defineTypes helpers (no decorators) avoid the problem.

concerns.message: Purity is not enforced by what the plan names. Leaving out the DOM lib does not remove `setTimeout`, `performance` and similar globals when `@types/node` sits hoisted at the root: TypeScript picks up every `@types/*` package unless `types: []` is set. An import-only purity test also cannot catch `Math.random`, `Date.now` or timers, because those are globals, not imports.
concerns.consequence: The purity unit test passes while a pure package calls `Math.random` or `setTimeout`, so the determinism guarantee the combat spike depends on is not actually checked. The pure packages' tsconfig needs `types: []`, and the purity test needs a source scan for those identifiers.

concerns.message: Movement tests can be flaky because of spawn slots and map bounds. §2 describes 'outer-world' spawn slots, and ships are clamped to the map. If the seeded generator puts the first ship at an edge and the e2e test presses toward that edge, the position does not change. In the same way, a 'one-input change' in the determinism test can land on a clamped ship, or on a non-world step that is never read, and produce the same hash.
concerns.consequence: two-ships-sync, or the hash-difference unit test, fails intermittently depending on the match seed. That is flakiness the verifier rejects, and it is hard to reproduce. Spawn slots should sit further inside the map than a test moves a ship, and tests should move toward the map centre.

concerns.message: 'Both ships are drawn on the canvas' has no specified way to be observed. With WebGL, `toDataURL` and `getImageData` read back blank unless `preserveDrawingBuffer` is set. Headless Chromium on a VPS without a GPU may not provide WebGL at all.
concerns.consequence: The worker either weakens the check to the DOM readout, which a reviewer will flag as not proving rendering, or writes pixel checks that pass locally and fail under the verifier. A small test hook that exposes the scene's ship sprites, or the Canvas renderer in tests, avoids both.

concerns.message: Playwright webServer on the fixed ports 2593 and 5393 with `reuseExistingServer: true`. If the worker leaves a dev server running, a later run reuses that stale process instead of starting the code under test.
concerns.consequence: Browser checks pass or fail against old code. The worker's own report.json can then disagree with the verifier's result.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Make every workspace package source-only: `exports` points at `src/index.ts`. Typecheck with `tsc -b` or per-workspace `tsc --noEmit`, run Vitest and Vite dev straight from source, and have `apps/server`'s build bundle its workspace dependencies (esbuild or Vite SSR) into one runnable `dist/index.js`. This removes the question of whether dist/ exists, for every check and for the Playwright web servers. For match codes, if filterBy's listing and locked-room behaviour gets in the way, set `this.roomId = code` in onCreate and join with `joinById(code.toUpperCase())`. That gives distinct errors for an unknown code and a full room, with no matchmaking filter at all. This conflicts with decisions.md, so only use it if the filterBy spike fails.
